userStories.intent: register a new book with a unique ISBN, title and author
userStories.benefit: the library catalog is kept accurate and no duplicate titles can be registered under the same ISBN

scenarios.given: the library catalog does not contain any book with ISBN '9783161484100'
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends POST /api/v1/books with body { "isbn": "9783161484100", "title": "Clean Code", "author": "Robert C. Martin" }
scenarios.then: the service persists the book with a generated UUID and createdAt timestamp and responds with HTTP 201 Created, a Location header '/api/v1/books/9783161484100' and the created representation including isbn, title and author

scenarios.given: a book with ISBN '9783161484100' already exists in the catalog
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends POST /api/v1/books with body { "isbn": "9783161484100", "title": "Another Title", "author": "Another Author" }
scenarios.then: the service does not create a second record and responds with HTTP 409 Conflict and errorCode 'BOOK_ISBN_DUPLICATE'

scenarios.given: the library catalog is available and the client is authenticated as Librarian
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends POST /api/v1/books with body { "isbn": "9783161484100", "title": "   ", "author": "Robert C. Martin" }
scenarios.then: the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request and a field-level validation error indicating that 'title' must not be blank

scenarios.when: the Librarian sends POST /api/v1/books with body { "isbn": "ABC-123", "title": "Clean Code", "author": "Robert C. Martin" }
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 400 Bad Request and a field-level validation error indicating that 'isbn' does not match the expected format

userStories.intent: update the title of an existing book identified by its ISBN
userStories.benefit: corrected or refined metadata is reflected in the catalog without changing the book identity

scenarios.given: a book with ISBN '9783161484100' and title 'Clean Code' exists in the catalog
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends PUT /api/v1/books/9783161484100 with body { "title": "Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship" }
scenarios.then: the service updates the stored title, sets updatedAt, leaves isbn and author unchanged and responds with HTTP 200 OK containing the updated representation

scenarios.given: no book with ISBN '9783161484100' exists in the catalog
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends PUT /api/v1/books/9783161484100 with body { "title": "Valid New Title" }
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 404 Not Found and errorCode 'BOOK_NOT_FOUND', and no record is created

scenarios.given: a book with ISBN '9783161484100' exists in the catalog
scenarios.when: the Librarian sends PUT /api/v1/books/9783161484100 with body { "title": "" }
scenarios.then: the service rejects the request with HTTP 400 Bad Request, the stored title remains 'Clean Code' and no updatedAt change is persisted

userStories.intent: retrieve a book by its ISBN to verify catalog integrity
userStories.benefit: catalog data can be inspected and audited without modifying any record

scenarios.given: a book with ISBN '9783161484100', title 'Clean Code' and author 'Robert C. Martin' exists in the catalog
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 200 OK and the full book representation including id, isbn, title, author and createdAt

scenarios.given: no book with ISBN '9780000000000' exists in the catalog
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 404 Not Found and errorCode 'BOOK_NOT_FOUND'

scenarios.given: the catalog is available and read access is granted
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 400 Bad Request and a validation error indicating that the ISBN format is invalid

userStories.intent: delete a book from the catalog by its ISBN
userStories.benefit: obsolete or incorrectly registered titles can be removed so the catalog stays reliable

scenarios.given: a book with ISBN '9783161484100' exists in the catalog
scenarios.then: the service removes the record and responds with HTTP 204 No Content, and a subsequent GET for that ISBN returns HTTP 404

scenarios.given: no book with ISBN '9783161484100' exists in the catalog
scenarios.then: the service responds with HTTP 404 Not Found and errorCode 'BOOK_NOT_FOUND' and the catalog remains unchanged
the service responds with HTTP 400 Bad Request and a validation error indicating that the ISBN format is invalid
